body:
### Problem

`test/issues/general/test_27205.test` returns too few rows from a hash join on the Windows 32-bit CI job, losing a varying number of build-side rows between runs (one run returned 15733800 instead of 15734000, another 15732800). It appeared after #28622 lowered the threshold for building a join hash table in parallel to 65536 rows: the failing query's build side has 78670 rows and the 4-core Windows runner now inserts into the table from several threads.

The parallel insert loop reads entries with `atomic<ht_entry_t>::load(std::memory_order_acquire)`. `ht_entry_t` is 8 bytes; on a 32-bit target the MSVC STL implements that load with `__iso_volatile_load64`, which clang-cl (the compiler of the Windows 32-bit job) lowers to two 32-bit `mov`s. A thread can therefore observe a half-written entry: the new pointer in the low half with the old salt still zero in the high half. It treats the entry as occupied with a non-matching salt, probes on, and starts a second chain for a key that already has one; the probe later finds only the first chain and the rows in the second one are silently dropped. With libstdc++ the same load is a single `fildll`, which is why 32-bit Linux builds do not show the problem; 64-bit targets load 8 bytes atomically.

### Fix

`LoadEntryConcurrent` reads an entry via `compare_exchange_strong(expected, expected)` when a pointer is narrower than an entry, which is a single `lock cmpxchg8b` and leaves the entry unchanged; 64-bit targets keep the plain acquire load. The two loads on the parallel insert path (the probe loop in `InsertHashesLoop<true>` and the expected-entry load in `InsertRowToEntry<true, false>`) use it. The single-threaded path is unchanged.

### Verification

- The torn load was confirmed by compiling the MSVC STL's 8-byte atomic load with `clang++ --target=i686-pc-windows-msvc -O2 -S`: the load is two 32-bit moves, the store likewise.
- 64-bit release build: `test_27205.test`, `test/sql/join/*` (205), `test/issues/general/*` (130) and `test/sql/parallelism/*` (79) pass.
- 32-bit Linux build with gcc on an x86 machine: `test_27205.test` passes 5/5 at 4 threads with and without the fix (libstdc++ loads atomically), `test/sql/join/*` passes apart from an out-of-memory in an ASOF slow test that fails identically without the fix (32-bit address space; not run by CI).
- The Windows 32-bit job of this PR is the real check; main's nightly passed that job once on 392cee07532, which is consistent with a race.

Note: this PR was generated by an AI coding agent and reviewed by the author.

comments.body: The PR's own run skips `windows / Windows (32 Bit)` (reduced matrix for a change outside `extension/`), so the job that showed the torn load is not exercised here; `windows / Windows (64 Bit)` and the Linux jobs pass. The code generation difference was confirmed offline by compiling the MSVC STL's 8-byte atomic load for `i686-pc-windows-msvc` with clang (two 32-bit moves) and the fix path on a 32-bit Linux build (test_27205 passes 5/5 at 4 threads). A full-matrix run (`OVERRIDE_REDUCED_CI_MODE: disabled` or a dispatch of the branch) would run the 32-bit job; the failure was reproducible on every attempt in the two runs that hit it, so a single green pass there would be meaningful.

Agreed, done in 0fada95f4e7: the compare-exchange read is now limited to `defined(_MSC_VER) && defined(_M_IX86)`, i.e. the MSVC STL on 32-bit x86, where the 8-byte `_Atomic_storage` load goes through `__iso_volatile_load64` and clang-cl lowers that intrinsic to two 32-bit moves. Everything else, including 32-bit libstdc++, ARM32 and wasm32, keeps the plain acquire load, so no other target pays for exclusive cache-line ownership on parallel-build probe steps. The condition is on the ABI/STL rather than on `__clang__` because the hazard is the STL's intrinsic plus the compiler's lowering of it; cl.exe emits a single 8-byte move and is unaffected, but keying on the STL path is the simplest condition that covers the broken combination.

Thanks, this answers my question. In `0fada95f4e7`, the `defined(_MSC_VER) && defined(_M_IX86)` guard covers clang-cl, keeps other targets on acquire loads and leaves x64/ARM64EC unchanged; the small extra cost for `cl.exe` seems reasonable. That leaves only a green Windows (32 Bit) CI run, which the reduced matrix skips; nothing else from my side.

Another occurrence without this fix: run 43102679623 on #26955 (which does not carry this change) failed `test/issues/general/test_27205.test:59` on Windows (32 Bit) with 15733800 rows instead of 15734000, on both retries. https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/actions/runs/43102679623/job/130814366974

review_comments.body: I would name clang-cl with the MSVC STL on x86 here, rather than suggest that 8-byte atomic loads can generally tear on 32-bit targets. A conforming `std::atomic` load is indivisible, however many instructions it takes. I would also explain that this read is a read-modify-write that preserves the value. This wording change need not block the PR.

Reworded in 0fada95f4e7: the comment now names the MSVC STL on 32-bit x86, whose 8-byte load goes through `__iso_volatile_load64` which clang-cl splits into two 32-bit moves, rather than implying 8-byte atomic loads can tear on 32-bit targets in general, and it states that the compare-exchange is a single read-modify-write that preserves the stored value (with `expected == desired` it either writes back the same empty entry or just loads the current one into `expected`).

This reads right now and resolves my point. Thanks for updating it.
